why: One block of markup with two authors: docs/index.html builds it in the browser when a card is sent, anki/fold_meaning.py builds it in Python for cards that already exist. They read their styles out of the same place, and this is what pins that down - a card folded on the phone and a card folded by the workflow have to be the same card.

info.meaning: a feeling of embarrassment or annoyance at having failed
info.nuance: Usually about your own failure, and usually mild.

confusables.difference: the adjective, and the more common form

examples: Much to her chagrin, the train left without her.
info.memory_hook: sha-GRIN: the grin you put on while you are quietly mortified.

in detail
a feeling of embarrassment or annoyance at having failed
/ʃəˈɡrɪn/ · formal, literary
Usually about your own failure, and usually mild.
goes with
much to my chagrin · to his chagrin
not to be confused with
chagrined — the adjective, and the more common form
